newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Babcock sells units to U.S. Tyco.
newsitem.headline: D.Babcock sells units to U.S. Tyco.

text.p: Troubled German engineering group Deutsche Babcock AG said on Monday it had sold fittings unit Babcock Sempell AG and its subsidiaries to the U.S. Tyco group.
In a regulatory news announcement Babcock said that the transaction had brought "a substantial inflow" of funds. No price was disclosed for the transaction, however.
Babcock Sempell, which employs around 1,150 workers, posted turnover in 1996 of over 215 million marks.
The deal comes hard on the heels of a leadership change at lossmaking Deutsche Babcock.

Klaus Lederer last week took over as chief executive from Heyo Schmiedeknecht, who was widely seen as responsible for an acquisition spree which dragged Babcock to major losses and strained credit lines in 1996.
The company made a group net loss of 434 million marks last year. Cash flow plunged to a negative 279 million marks.
